{"metadata":{"description":"Makes the branch the building block of AI conversation management — parallel workflows, continuous and mergeable conversation memory","id":"gh:1340820702","install_available":false,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-session-fork","slug":"Jason-skd/dsh-session-fork","topics":["ai-agents","branch","deepseek","deepseek-harness","dsh","dsh-plugin","session-management"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Makes the branch the building block of AI conversation management — parallel workflows, continuous a"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"nd mergeable conversation memory"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-session-fork"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"English | 简体中文"},{"id":"p4s1","text":"`dsh-session-fork` brings a Git-like branch model to `DeepSeek Harness`, making it possible to work "},{"id":"p4s2","text":"on several large, relatively independent tasks in parallel across dsh sessions."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Instead of keeping every task in one linear conversation, each task can evolve in its own branch. Wh"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"en the work is ready to come together, `squash` and `rebase` provide ways to bring the work back int"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"o a unified history."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"This is a plugin for `DeepSeek Harness`; it cannot run standalone."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"Version `0.4.0` supports dsh `0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.3`, `0.2.1-rc.4`, and `0.2.2-rc.1`. It replaces"},{"id":"p7s2","text":" the previous dsh `0.1.2-rc.1` compatibility line; upgrade dsh before upgrading this plugin."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"For compatibility development, build a sibling `../deepseek-harness` checkout and run `bun run test:"},{"id":"p8s2","text":"harness`. Set `DSH_HARNESS_DIR` to use another checkout. The check uses an isolated copy linked to t"},{"id":"p8s3","text":"he actual harness packages and checks V4 messages, historical merges, and both Host and Client types"},{"id":"p8s4","text":"e actual harness packages and checks V4 messages, historical merges, and both Host and Client types."},{"id":"p9s1","text":"## Why branches for parallel development?"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"The branch model mirrors how programmers already handle parallel work with Git."},{"id":"p11s1","text":"When several large tasks are being developed in parallel, each branch can evolve independently witho"},{"id":"p11s2","text":"ut requiring every change to be resolved immediately. Once the work is ready, branches can be brough"},{"id":"p11s3","text":"t back together through operations such as `squash` and `rebase`."},{"id":"p12s1","text":"This provides a mapping from:"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"**parallel development → unified history**"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"The goal is to make parallel development practical while keeping the ability to bring the resulting "},{"id":"p14s2","text":"work back into a coherent history."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Branches are not sub-agents"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"Branches and sub-agents solve different problems."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"A branch is intended for several large, relatively unrelated tasks that need to progress independent"},{"id":"p17s2","text":"ly. It is not simply a way to split one large task into several smaller tasks."},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Sub-agents are still useful for small, lightweight tasks. They can be cheaper in context and better "},{"id":"p18s2","text":"suited to work that does not need an independent long-running session."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"The two approaches can also coexist. Sub-agents can remain part of the workflow, while branches prov"},{"id":"p19s2","text":"ide a clearer boundary for larger parallel tasks."},{"id":"p20s1","text":"## Keep thinking while your agents work"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"One practical motivation for the project is to reduce the waiting time that can happen when working "},{"id":"p21s2","text":"with a single agent session."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"There is a familiar joke about vibe coding being:"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"> chat once, then spend ten minutes on your phone."},{"id":"p24s1","text":"Parallel branches make it possible to continue working on other tasks instead of waiting for one con"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"versation to finish before moving on."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"In the maintainer's experience, roughly **5× the token consumption produced roughly 4× the efficienc"},{"id":"p25s2","text":"he maintainer's experience, roughly **5× the token consumption produced roughly 4× the efficiency**."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"The trade-off is additional token usage in exchange for keeping development moving across multiple t"},{"id":"p26s2","text":"rade-off is additional token usage in exchange for keeping development moving across multiple tasks."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"## Let AI handle session management"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"Independent sessions are harder to manage than sub-agents."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"They are not inherently bound to the main session, and their lifecycle and identity are more difficu"},{"id":"p29s2","text":"lt to keep track of. dsh-session-fork addresses this by providing:"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"- A complete set of branch management commands.
- Agent-callable tool versions of those commands.
- "},{"id":"p30s2","text":"A recommended governance approach for managing branch sessions."},{"id":"p31s1","text":"The goal is that developers do not need to manually worry about the details of session management. T"},{"id":"p31s2","text":"he AI can handle the branch lifecycle and orchestration while the developer focuses on the work."},{"id":"p32s1","text":"## DeepSeek Harness integration"},{"id":"p33s1","text":"dsh-session-fork is designed to work with dsh's existing features rather than creating a separate se"},{"id":"p33s2","text":" is designed to work with dsh's existing features rather than creating a separate session ecosystem."},{"id":"p34s1","text":"The project follows a pattern-mimic and vendor approach to integration with dsh."},{"id":"p35s1","text":"For example, a `squash` operation produces a summary message that remains compatible with dsh's `com"},{"id":"p35s2","text":"pact`-style summary behavior."},{"id":"p36s1","text":"Sub-agents can also continue to work alongside the branch-based workflow."},{"id":"p37s1","text":"## AI secretary direction"},{"id":"p38s1","text":"The branch model also opens the possibility of an **AI secretary** workflow."},{"id":"p39s1","text":"A root branch can maintain a board and a clean context while the AI coordinates the developer's curr"},{"id":"p39s2","text":"ent tasks and handles the connections between them."},{"id":"p40s1","text":"The secretary can organise the developer's workflow and habits while retaining the operational capab"},{"id":"p40s2","text":"ilities needed to manage the development process."},{"id":"p41s1","text":"The longer-term direction is for the AI to focus on task orchestration and coordination while the de"},{"id":"p41s2","text":"veloper focuses on the current work."},{"id":"p42s1","text":"This is part of the project's **v0.3.0 AI secretary** direction."},{"id":"p43s1","text":"## Quick start"},{"id":"p44s1","text":"Install (requires a web-app-based dsh profile):"},{"id":"p45s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p46s1","text":"After that, let your agent use the plugin freely. Every command also ships as an agent-callable tool"},{"id":"p46s2","text":"fter that, let your agent use the plugin freely. Every command also ships as an agent-callable tool."},{"id":"p47s1","text":"## Core features"},{"id":"p48s1","text":"- `branch` operations give every session a name, an ancestry, and an index, with commands for managi"},{"id":"p48s2","text":"ng them.
- `fork` strengthens the native experience and provides the ancestry primitive.
- `squash` "},{"id":"p48s3","text":"and `rebase` provide two forms of cross-branch merging.
- `send_message_by_branch` strengthens commu"},{"id":"p48s4","text":"nication between sessions.
- The **branch** tab provides visual management of branches."},{"id":"p49s1","text":"## Join us"},{"id":"p50s1","text":"What we want to build next:"},{"id":"p51s1","text":"1. **Branch-scoped project memory**. Existing long-term memory models are project-grained, which can"},{"id":"p51s2","text":" cause memory to leak across branches and pollute context. Branch-grained memory management is inten"},{"id":"p51s3","text":"ded to make the model more robust.
2. **Ongoing maintenance**. Open `Issues` to find long-term impro"},{"id":"p51s4","text":"vements and bugs waiting for contributions."},{"id":"p52s1","text":"We take an open stance on AI collaboration: feel free to use AI to contribute code, write commit mes"},{"id":"p52s2","text":"sages, and draft PRs. But we expect you to own your code, review it yourself, and treat AI as your t"},{"id":"p52s3","text":"ool in communication rather than letting it talk to us on your behalf."},{"id":"p53s1","text":"## License"},{"id":"p54s1","text":"MIT"}],"truncated":false}
